title: Self-Contained Attack Invoke — Plug & Play Attack Lifecycle
why: Firing an attack macro today requires the CALLER to know which host owns its lifecycle and to pass a fully-wired ctx. Barrel payloads, enemies, and bosses each hand-roll step/draw wiring (or silently skip it), so every new object/enemy/boss that fires a macro needs bespoke glue and can silently fail to render or tick. This is not extensible.
outcomes: invoke() + trigger become self-contained: any caller fires any macro in one line and the engine guarantees it is stepped, drawn, and pruned automatically. No per-caller host wiring. New attacks plug in with zero lifecycle code. Latent unstepped-payload bugs (e.g. enemy explosion/shockwave) are fixed for free.

milestones.name: Attack Lifecycle Registry
milestones.objective: A single engine-owned registry that auto-tracks every live attack handle and drives its step/draw/prune in one place, so invoke() never abandons a handle.
milestones.success: Any handle returned by invoke() is stepped, drawn, and pruned by the game loop with zero caller code. No double-stepping of host-owned roots.
milestones.diagram:
graph TD
  A[caller invokes macro] --> B[invoke returns handle]
  B --> C{handle has step or zone}
  C|yes| D[auto-register into AttackLifecycle]
  C|no instant| E[skip - completes synchronously]
  D --> F[game loop steps all live handles]
  F --> G{handle done}
  G|no| H[draw zones each frame]
  G|yes| I[self-prune from registry]

tasks.name: AttackLifecycle registry module
tasks.what: Add js/combat/attack/lifecycle.js: a Set of live handles with register(h), stepAll(dt, targets), drawAll(ctx), and clear(). A handle is 'live' when it has a .step fn or a .zone; it self-prunes once _completed/_cancelled.
tasks.why: This is the single engine-owned lifecycle owner that replaces every per-caller host/ad-hoc step-draw path.
acceptance: register() ignores already-completed handles and handles with no step/zone
stepAll() calls h.step(dt, targets) on each live handle exactly once and prunes completed ones
drawAll() recursively draws h.zone for the handle and every nested h.handles entry
clear() cancels all live handles and empties the set

tasks.name: Ownership tag to prevent double-stepping
tasks.what: Add an opt-out so a handle already owned by a host (bombAttacks) is not double-stepped by the registry. Registering marks h._lifecycleOwned; host-owned roots either skip registration or set the flag so stepAll() skips them.
tasks.why: bombAttacks.step() already drives hero-shot roots; if the registry also steps them, carriers get double physics and payloads fire twice. Ownership must be explicit and unambiguous.
acceptance: a host-owned root registered with owned=true is drawn but NOT stepped by stepAll
a registry-owned handle is both stepped and drawn
no handle is ever stepped twice in one frame (assert via a counting stub)

milestones.name: Self-Registering Invoke
milestones.objective: Wire invoke() to auto-register live handles into the registry, and make the game loop drive the registry instead of the ad-hoc per-caller paths.
milestones.success: barrelSync propane fan, toxic zones, and enemy payloads all flow through the registry. The hand-rolled setBombHostGetter / barrelAttackRoots / stepToxicZones wiring is removed.
milestones.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Caller
  participant Invoke
  participant Registry
  participant Loop
  Caller->>Invoke: invoke(id, params, ctx)
  Invoke->>Invoke: build handle
  Invoke->>Registry: register(handle) if live
  Invoke-->>Caller: handle
  Loop->>Registry: stepAll(dt)
  Registry->>Registry: h.step for each live
  Loop->>Registry: drawAll(ctx)
  Registry->>Registry: h.zone.draw for each live
  Registry->>Registry: prune completed

tasks.name: invoke() auto-registers live handles
tasks.what: In engine.js invoke(), after the handle is built, call AttackLifecycle.register(handle) for any non-completed handle that needs driving. Host-spawned roots (bombAttacks.spawn) register with owned=true so they are drawn but not double-stepped.
tasks.why: This is the plug-and-play core: from now on a bare invoke() can never silently drop a handle's lifecycle.
acceptance: a bare invoke() of a duration macro (e.g. fireArea) appears in AttackLifecycle._live without caller code
an instant macro that completes synchronously is NOT left in the registry
bombAttacks.spawn roots are present for drawing but carry _registryStepped=false

tasks.name: Game loop drives the registry
tasks.what: In systems/update.js call AttackLifecycle.stepAll(dt, getDamageables()) once per frame (after the pool-resident stepBomb pass and bombAttacks.step). In systems/render.js call AttackLifecycle.drawAll(ctx) in world space. Remove stepToxicZones/drawToxicZones and setBombHostGetter from the loop.
tasks.why: One step + one draw call replaces every bespoke per-caller lifecycle path, which is the whole point of self-containment.
acceptance: toxic dust zones still tick damage and expire via the registry (no stepToxicZones call remains)
propane molotov fire zones render with no barrelSync-specific draw code
setBombHostGetter is no longer referenced by the game loop

tasks.name: barrelSync fires macros with zero lifecycle wiring
tasks.what: Rewrite the propane and toxic branches in barrelSync to a bare invoke() (or ctx.bombAttacks.spawn for hero-aligned) and drop the _getBombHost/setBombHostGetter, spawnToxicDustZone, stepToxicZones, drawToxicZones helpers. The registry now owns their step/draw.
tasks.why: This is the concrete proof of the goal: the caller that previously needed host + getter + 3 helper functions now needs one line.
acceptance: propane fan spawns 5 molotov lobes that render fire on the floor with only an invoke() call
toxic cloud ticks damage and expires with only an invoke() call
no reference to setBombHostGetter, _getBombHost, spawnToxicDustZone, stepToxicZones, or drawToxicZones remains in barrelSync

milestones.name: Host Unification & Migration
milestones.objective: Collapse the parallel host/registry paths so there is ONE lifecycle owner. Migrate hero shots, barrel payloads, and enemy/boss payloads onto it, then delete the bespoke wiring.
milestones.success: bombAttacks either becomes a thin adapter over the registry or is removed. No caller references setBombHostGetter, barrelAttackRoots, or stepToxicZones. Full test suite green at baseline.

tasks.name: Migrate enemy + boss payloads to bare invoke
tasks.what: Change explosiveMonkey.detonate (and any boss payload that stores a _payloadHandle) to a plain invoke() with no stored handle and no manual step. The registry steps/draws the explosion/shockwave automatically.
tasks.why: These are the latent unstepped-payload bugs: today _payloadHandle is stored but never stepped, so enemy blasts rely on side effects. The registry fixes them for free.
acceptance: an exploding monkey's blast ticks damage over its duration (was previously unstepped)
no enemy/boss stores an attack handle solely to step it by hand

tasks.name: Decide bombAttacks fate: adapter or removal
tasks.what: Either reduce bombAttackHost to a thin ctx-factory + owned-root marker (registry does step/draw) OR fold its groundY/platforms/camera ctx into the shared context and delete the host. Keep hero-shot behavior identical.
tasks.why: Two lifecycle owners is the exact smell we are removing; this task forces a single owner while preserving hero-shot correctness.
acceptance: hero bombs/homing/explosive shots behave identically to before (existing shooting tests pass)
exactly one component calls h.step for any given handle per frame

tasks.name: Delete dead wiring + verify baseline
tasks.what: Remove now-dead exports (setBombHostGetter, spawnToxicDustZone, stepToxicZones, drawToxicZones, barrelAttackRoots if any remain) and their imports. Run the full suite and confirm the pre-existing failure count is unchanged (no new failures).
tasks.why: Leaving dead lifecycle paths behind recreates the confusion; a clean grep proves there is one owner.
acceptance: grep for the removed symbols returns zero non-test hits
full test suite shows the same pass/fail counts as the pre-change baseline (6 pre-existing failures, nothing new)

milestones.name: Guards & Regression Net
milestones.objective: Make the self-contained guarantee provable: a test that any macro fired from a bare ctx renders and ticks, plus a lint-style guard against discarded live handles.
milestones.success: A new attack added to the registry passes the plug-and-play test with no caller wiring. The suite catches any future handle that is invoked but never stepped/drawn.

tasks.name: Plug-and-play contract test
tasks.what: Add js/test/attackLifecycle.test.js: for a set of representative macros (fireArea, molotov via spawnSplit, dustZone, shockwave), fire each from a minimal bare ctx and assert the registry stepped it >=1x, drew its zone >=1x, and pruned it after completion - with NO caller wiring.
tasks.why: This is the executable definition of 'self-contained'. Any future macro that breaks the guarantee fails here immediately instead of in gameplay.
acceptance: each sample macro is stepped, drawn, and pruned with zero caller lifecycle code
a deliberately non-driving handle (no step/zone) is not registered

tasks.name: Discarded-handle guard test
tasks.what: Add a test that scans for the anti-pattern: an invoke() of a duration macro whose handle is neither registered, host-owned, nor explicitly completed. Fail with the file:line if a live handle is dropped.
tasks.why: This catches the exact bug class that cost this session - a macro fired and abandoned - before it reaches gameplay.
acceptance: firing the propane fan registers its molotov children (not discarded)
firing an enemy explosion registers or completes the payload (not silently dropped)

tasks.name: Document the self-contained invoke contract
tasks.what: Add a short section to docs/architecture (attack engine) stating the one rule: callers fire via invoke() and never wire step/draw; the registry owns lifecycle. Note the single exception (host-owned roots) and how to add a new macro.
tasks.why: The convention only sticks if it is written down where the next person looks.
snippet:
# Attack Lifecycle - Self-Contained Invoke
## The one rule
Callers fire attacks with invoke(id, params, ctx). They NEVER step or draw
the handle. AttackLifecycle (engine-owned) steps, draws, and prunes every
live handle automatically.
## Adding a new macro
1. Register it (primitive or macro) with meta.effects.
2. If it needs per-frame driving, give its handle a .step fn or a .zone.
3. Done. No host, no getter, no game-loop edit.
## Single exception
Host-owned roots (hero shots via bombAttacks) set _registryStepped=false so
the registry draws them but the host steps them. One owner, always.
acceptance: the doc states the one-rule contract and the single host-owned exception
a 'how to add a new macro' section exists with 3 steps and no lifecycle wiring
